title: What your exhaust smoke color is telling you
negativePromptStanding: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.label: hook
beats.vo: Exhaust smoke color is a clue.
beats.prompt: Close-up static shot of a car exhaust tailpipe at idle in a dim shop bay, faint haze in the air, shallow depth of field, realistic automotive documentary lighting, no visible smoke yet

beats.label: blue-smoke
beats.vo: Blue-gray smoke usually points to oil getting into the engine and burning off — often worn valve seals or piston rings.
beats.prompt: Close-up slow-motion shot of thick blue-gray smoke puffing rhythmically from a car exhaust pipe against dark wet asphalt, cool overcast light, realistic vapor texture, shallow depth of field

beats.label: white-smoke
beats.vo: Thick white smoke that doesn't clear after warm-up can point to coolant getting into the engine — that one shouldn't wait.
beats.prompt: Close-up shot of thick white smoke billowing continuously from a car exhaust pipe in cold shop-bay air, dense opaque vapor, moody fluorescent garage lighting, realistic texture

beats.label: black-smoke-cta
beats.vo: Black smoke usually means the engine's running rich, burning more fuel than it should — worth having someone check, not a guess.
beats.prompt: Close-up shot of black sooty smoke puffing from an exhaust pipe during hard acceleration on a city street, gritty high-contrast look, slight handheld drift, realistic exhaust soot texture

beats.label: save-freeze
beats.prompt: Wide static shot of a tire and auto repair shop bay with the door open, organized tools and a lift in the background, warm inviting late-afternoon light, empty of people, held completely still for a 3-second freeze
beats.ctaText: Worth checking, not guessing. Stop by and we'll take a look. Nick's Tire & Auto · 17625 Euclid Ave, Cleveland
